channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Após aprovação de Daniel Perez pelo Senado dos EUA, governo Lula mantém posição de analisar indicação depois das eleições
item.description: The Lula government maintains its stance of waiting until after Brazil's 2026 presidential elections to analyze the nomination of Daniel Perez as U.S. ambassador to Brazil, viewing the U.S. Senate's approval as part of a pressure campaign. Brazil's refusal to grant agrément immediately is seen as a response to the lack of prior consultation by the U.S. and the revocation of the Brazilian ambassador's visa in Washington, which has deepened the diplomatic crisis.

item.title: Missão oficializa 128 candidaturas para deputado e deixa em aberto apoio a governo e Senado por SP
item.description: The Mission party officially registered 128 candidacies for the 2026 proportional elections: 71 for state deputy and 57 for federal deputy, including 28 women for the São Paulo State Legislature and 21 for the Chamber of Deputies. While it has nominated Renan Santos for president, the party has not yet decided whether to run or support candidates for governor of São Paulo and senator, with the decision still under analysis. Party conventions could be held until August 5, with candidate registration at the Electoral Justice allowed until August 15.

item.title: Lula diz que mandará ‘foto’ para Trump de dados que mostram a queda do desmatamento no Brasil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he wants to send a photo of INPE data showing Brazil’s deforestation decline to U.S. President Donald Trump, as a rebuttal to U.S. tariffs justified by claims that Brazilian goods gain unfair advantage through environmental crimes. Lula accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of being a 'bolsonarista' and 'anti-Latino-American,' claiming Rubio hindered negotiations over the tariffs. Despite the tensions, Lula noted he was treated respectfully by Trump at the White House and stressed that the two largest democracies share a duty to maintain harmony.

item.title: Dani Lima: Flávio dá pedra e vidraça a adversários ao escalar Gaspar vice
item.description: The selection of Alfredo Gaspar as running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro on the PL ticket for the 2026 elections exposes the campaign to predictable wear and provides ammunition to opponents, according to columnist Daniela Lima on UOL News. The move is seen as strategic but risky, given Gaspar’s background and potential vulnerabilities.

item.title: Sakamoto: Fé menor de eleitor de Flávio pode compensar abstenção lulista
item.description: Lower confidence among Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) electorate in his candidate's victory could help reduce abstention among Lula's (PT) voters, according to Leonardo Sakamoto's analysis on UOL News. This dynamic might benefit Lula by mitigating one of his campaign's main risks: low turnout from his base.

item.title: Val Marchiori nega patrimônio de R$ 49 milhões e explica declaração
item.description: Val Marchiori, a federal deputy candidate for São Paulo from the Republicans party, denied having a R$ 49 million assets after a typo in her asset declaration submitted to the TSE, where a R$ 482,000 property was mistakenly recorded as R$ 48 million. The party stated it will correct the filing, updating her net worth to R$ 1,419,778.21. This is her first electoral run.

item.title: Lula diz que vai enviar a Trump gráficos sobre queda do desmatamento
item.description: Lula said he would send charts showing Brazil's decline in deforestation to Donald Trump, criticizing the U.S. stance on climate issues. He also called Marco Rubio a 'frustrated Latin American' and asserted that Brazil takes climate change more seriously than other nations. The U.S. cited the 2021 deforestation peak under Bolsonaro to justify new trade tariffs.

item.title: Ao TSE, Renan Santos declara patrimônio de R$ 795 mil. Veja os bens
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) filed his candidacy for President of Brazil with the TSE, declaring assets worth R$ 795 thousand, including other credits and savings (R$ 300k), capital quotas (R$ 100k), other corporate holdings (R$ 119,760), and assets related to self-employed activity (R$ 275,329). His 'Livro Amarelo' government plan proposes replacing Bolsa Família, merging municipalities from 5,570 to 1,656 ('Great Municipal Consolidation'), combating organized crime with superprisons, and covering economy, public security, health, education, and culture.

item.title: ESPECIAL: Natuza Nery e Andréia Sadi entrevistam Ronaldo Caiado - O Assunto #1778
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD presidential candidate, proposed amnesty for those convicted of the January 8 acts, a unified police force for South American nations to combat transnational crime, and immediate submission of administrative, political, and tax reform proposals on his first day in office, alongside discussions on a new pension reform. He ruled out privatizing Banco do Brasil and Caixa, emphasizing fiscal adjustment and national pacification.

item.title: Senado dos EUA aprova Daniel Perez como novo embaixador no Brasil
item.description: The U.S. Senate confirmed Daniel Perez as the new U.S. ambassador to Brazil with a 51-47 vote. The nomination sparked a diplomatic crisis after the Trump administration announced the pick before completing confidential consultations, prompting the U.S. to revoke the visa of Brazil’s ambassador to Washington, Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti. Brazil’s Itamaraty must still grant agrément for Perez to assume the post, which has been vacant since January 2025.

item.title: A empresários, Flávio critica Lula e promete governo "moderno"
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL presidential candidate, met with business leaders in São Caetano do Sul (SP), where he criticized the 2023 tax reform, pledged to halt its implementation and reassess rules under a potential government, and attacked Lula for failing to improve national indicators across three terms. He promoted a 'modern' government focused on the future, aligned with his campaign's 'Brazil of the Future' narrative, and emphasized São Paulo’s strategic importance, where polls show a technical tie with Lula in the first round.

item.title: TSE reúne YouTube e influenciadores digitais em ação estratégica contra a desinformação
item.description: The TSE held a virtual meeting with YouTube representatives and digital influencers to combat misinformation ahead of the 2026 General Elections. The discussion centered on simplifying institutional language and strengthening joint actions to clarify the electoral system and counter false narratives about vote counting.

item.title: PL reserva Avenida Paulista no 7 de Setembro para comício de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) has reserved Avenida Paulista in São Paulo for a campaign rally by Flávio Bolsonaro on September 7, 2026, a date symbolic for Bolsonaro supporters. The event is expected to launch his presidential campaign, which will also include a kickoff in Rio de Janeiro and a visit to Maceió, the hometown of his chosen running mate, Alfredo Gaspar. Avenida Paulista has been a frequent stage for right-wing demonstrations, including the 2021 event where Jair Bolsonaro defied the Supreme Court.

item.title: Zema declara patrimônio de R$ 178,7 milhões ao registrar candidatura ao Planalto no TSE
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential candidate for the Novo party, declared a net worth of R$ 178.7 million when registering his candidacy with the TSE, a 38% increase from his 2022 declaration. The bulk of his assets is tied to a family holding (R$ 94.5 million), followed by an investment fund (R$ 56.2 million) and a stake in a financial institution (R$ 16.8 million). Despite his growing wealth, Zema polls at only 2% in the Genial/Quaest survey, while Lula leads with 40%.

item.title: Renan Santos divulga patrimônio
item.description: Renan Santos, national president of Missão and pre-candidate for President of Brazil, declared to the Electoral Justice a patrimony of 795,080 reais. The amount includes 275,320 reais in assets related to self-employment, 119,760 reais from corporate participation, and 100,000 reais in quotas, among other unspecified assets.

item.title: EUA diz que respeitará escolha do Brasil em “eleições livres e justas”
item.description: The United States stated it will respect the Brazilian people's choice in free and fair elections, amid rising diplomatic tensions with the Lula government. The comment followed Brazil's denial of visas to three U.S. officials seeking to scrutinize the electoral system. Meanwhile, the Trump administration revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador to the U.S. and approved Daniel Perez as the new U.S. ambassador to Brazil, though Brazil's agrément — required for his appointment — is unlikely before the 2026 elections.

item.title: PCO confirma Rui Costa Pimenta como candidato à Presidência
item.description: The Workers' Cause Party (PCO) confirmed Rui Costa Pimenta as its presidential candidate for the 2026 elections during a national convention in Brasília. Pimenta, a journalist and writer, is running for president for the fifth time, having previously contested in 2002, 2006, 2010, and 2014. The party will run a 'pure-blood' ticket with Antônio Carlos Silva as vice-presidential candidate, stating the campaign aims to organize and mobilize workers with a program independent of the bourgeoisie.

item.title: Flávio critica reforma tributária em almoço com empresários do ABC
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) lunched with around 80 businesspeople from the ABC Paulista region and criticized the tax reform approved during Lula's government, stating he voted against the bill in the Senate. He also attacked the petista government's economic policy, citing high household debt, high interest rates, and national impoverishment, signaling that if elected, he will prioritize spending cuts.

item.title: Caiado diz que privatizaria segmentos do gás, mas não Petrobras, Banco do Brasil e Caixa
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado stated he would not privatize Petrobras, Banco do Brasil, or Caixa Econômica Federal, but admitted he would consider privatizing segments of the gas sector if elected. The remarks were made during a GloboNews interview on Friday, April 7. Caiado aims to balance defending strategic state-owned enterprises with pursuing sector-specific economic reforms.

item.title: Caiado diz que não faria retaliação aos Estados Unidos em razão do tarifaço
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado stated he would not retaliate against the United States over the tariff hike, arguing that such a move could lead to the loss of U.S. investments in Brazil. The remarks were made during a GloboNews interview on Friday, the 7th.

item.title: Centrais sindicais farão pressão sobre o Senado contra escala 6x1
item.description: Brazilian trade unions have launched a leaflet campaign to pressure the Senate into voting on a constitutional amendment (PEC) to abolish the 6x1 work schedule before the October elections. The initiative aims to ensure the proposal is debated and approved in the legislative chamber, responding to a long-standing workers’ demand for a reduced weekly workload.

item.title: Nova lei autoriza polícia a fazer rondas virtuais nas redes para investigar abuso de menores
item.description: President Lula signed a law authorizing police and the Public Prosecutor’s Office to conduct virtual patrols on social media to investigate sexual crimes against children and adolescents, including AI-generated deepfakes. The law permits infiltration of closed groups on platforms like WhatsApp and Telegram, allows direct requests to digital platforms to identify suspects without prior judicial authorization (with notification to the judiciary within 48 hours), and increases penalties: 4 to 10 years for producing child sexual abuse material, with higher sentences if material is sold or committed by relatives/neighbors, and 3 to 5 years for creating, distributing, or storing deepfakes depicting minors in sexual acts.

item.title: Renan Santos ultrapassa Lula e encosta em Flávio em índice de impacto digital
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) surpassed Lula in the Brazil Digital Impact Index (iBR), marking the first time he has outperformed the former president in Instagram performance. He also significantly narrowed the gap with Flávio Bolsonaro, the current leader of the index. An unprecedented DSC LAB survey shows a notable increase in Renan Santos’ digital presence in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Crusoé: Veja os luxos de Erika Hilton que superam o patrimônio declarado
item.description: The Crusoé article criticizes federal deputy Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP) for allegedly displaying luxury goods, such as a designer bag, whose value exceeds the assets she declared to the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), which amount to only R$ 15.985,73. The publication suggests a discrepancy between her apparent lifestyle on social media and her official asset declaration, implying possible underreporting or inconsistency.

item.title: 'Milei e Trump compartilham antipatia por Lula e ficariam satisfeitos com eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro'
item.description: Diplomatic tensions between Brazil, the United States, and Argentina have risen following allegations of electoral interference, controversial remarks by Milei against Lula, and the revocation of the Brazilian ambassador’s U.S. visa. Analysts suggest Trump and Milei may favor Flávio Bolsonaro’s victory over Lula in the 2026 elections, though no direct coordination has been proven. The situation reflects a right-wing ideological alignment viewing Lula as a political opponent.

item.title: Caiado sobre tarifaço: ‘Eu, retaliar os americanos? Para acabar com o resto das exportações?’
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD presidential candidate, rejected retaliating against the United States over the tariff hike, arguing it would harm Brazilian exports and lose American investments. He advocated for high-level talks with Donald Trump, emphasizing Brazil’s competitive edge in rare earths and niobium, and stated the Itamaraty would no longer be an ideological arm of the PT. Caiado also refused to negotiate Pix, calling it a 'national sentiment'.

item.title: Moro nega ser adversário de Ratinho Jr., minimiza passado de Valdemar e acusa Lula de interferir na PF
item.description: Sergio Moro (PL) stated he is not an adversary of Governor Ratinho Jr. (PSD) and pledged to continue his projects if elected governor of Paraná, while downplaying Valdemar Costa Neto's (PL) past, saying he 'already paid for his mistakes'. Moro also accused President Lula (PT) of interfering in the Federal Police to benefit his son, Fábio Luís, and of attempting to obstruct investigations in the INSS CPMI.

item.title: Caiado diz que "governa" com emendas e considera facções terroristas
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD-GO), presidential candidate, stated he would govern 'tranquilly' with parliamentary amendments but insisted they must align with the Executive's plan, criticizing the current system as a destabilization of presidentialism. On security, he proposed classifying criminal factions as 'domestic terrorists' on his first day to deploy the Armed Forces in the Amazon and create a transnational police force with Brazil's ten neighboring countries. He accused the Lula government of being complicit in narcotrafficking and opposed body cameras for military police.

item.title: Superpresídio, Bolsa Família e mais: o que diz o plano de Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from the Missão party, presented the 'Yellow Book' with proposals including merging municipalities by up to 70% (from 5,570 to 1,656), replacing Bolsa Família with forced labor programs, and creating superprisons. The plan also includes a public security policy based on the motto 'Prendeu, Matou', treating criminals as enemies of the State. These measures aim to reduce costs, combat organized crime, and reform welfare assistance.

item.title: Entrevista ao g1 e à GloboNews: Caiado descarta privatizar BB e Caixa e propõe ajuste fiscal e revisão da reforma tributária
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), presidential candidate, advocates for fiscal adjustment through public spending cuts and a revision of the tax reform to reduce bureaucracy. He proposes privatizing Correios and segments of Petrobras, particularly in natural gas exploration, but rules out privatizing Banco do Brasil and Caixa Econômica Federal due to their role in serving disadvantaged regions. Caiado cited his experience in Goiás, where he implemented administrative reforms, cut fiscal incentives by over R$3 billion, and reformed the state pension system.

item.title: Caiado quer anistiar condenados pelo 8 de Janeiro: “Pacificar o país”
item.description: Presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) stated that, if elected, he would send to Congress on the first day of his government a bill granting amnesty to those convicted of the January 8 attacks, aiming to "pacify the country" and remove the issue from political debate. He likened the measure to the annulment of Lula’s convictions, which allowed the former president to run again, and said the amnesty would be part of a broader reform package including administrative, political, tax, and pension changes. Caiado did not directly label the January 8 events as a coup attempt but asserted that, under his administration, acts of destruction would not be tolerated.

item.title: Fim da escala 6×1: Boulos diz que Lula e Alcolumbre não têm acordo e que PEC não pode ‘morrer na praia’
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (PSOL) stated that President Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre have not yet reached an agreement on the PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule, which remains stalled in Congress. He urged that the proposal be voted on before the October elections to prevent it from 'dying on the beach,' noting that over 70% of Brazilians support the measure according to Datafolha. Boulos condemned lawmakers who pretend the PEC does not exist, calling it a mockery of the working class.

item.title: Mercadante prepara entrada na campanha e amplia time econômico de Lula
item.description: Aloizio Mercadante, president of the BNDES, plans to take a vacation in September to informally support Lula’s reelection campaign, focusing on economic policy formulation and political coordination. This marks a shift from the initial plan to request a leave of absence from the BNDES, as Mercadante argues he can contribute more by staying in office, leveraging the bank’s institutional platform to highlight government investments and counter opposition narratives—particularly in São Paulo, where the BNDES funds projects like the Santos-Guarujá tunnel.

item.title: Nabil Bonduki lança livro sobre a 'corda bamba' do urbanismo brasileiro
item.description: São Paulo city councilor Nabil Bonduki (PT), a pre-candidate for federal deputy, will launch his book 'Urbanism on a Tightrope' this Saturday (8) at Flipei (Independent Publishers Literary Festival). The work addresses the challenges of Brazilian urbanism, focusing on tensions between sustainable development and political and economic pressures.

item.title: Lu Alckmin ensina o PT a usar vermelho na campanha em que marqueteiros querem ‘desavermelhar’ Lula
item.description: Lu Alckmin, wife of Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, drew attention at the PT convention by wearing a red dress, countering the campaign's effort to 'de-red' Lula's image to appeal to moderate voters. Her choice was praised as a symbol of joy and unity, despite criticism from the party's left wing that prefers to maintain the traditional red identity. While strategists push green, yellow, and white to counter Bolsonaro's appropriation of national colors, Lu Alckmin defends red as an expression of collective positivity and partnership in the campaign.

item.title: Zema registra candidatura ao Planalto e declara patrimônio de R$ 178,7 milhões
item.description: Romeu Zema of the Novo party formally registered his 2026 presidential candidacy, declaring a net worth of R$178.7 million, placing him among the wealthiest presidential candidates in Brazilian history. His assets are primarily held in family holdings, multimarket funds, and financial institutions, reflecting his business background prior to politics. Zema aims to position himself as a distinct liberal right-wing alternative to both Lula and Bolsonaro-aligned forces, leveraging his Minas Gerais governance record as an administrative showcase.

item.title: Renan Santos registra candidatura à Presidência e declara patrimônio de R$ 795 mil
item.description: Businessman Renan Santos (Missão) registered his presidential candidacy with a declared net worth of R$795,000, with reserve military police officer Aroldo Medina as his running mate. His government plan proposes ending the quota system, replacing Bolsa Família with work fronts, implementing fiscal adjustment including decoupling social benefits from the minimum wage, and merging the Culture and Education ministries. So far, only Renan Santos, Romeu Zema (Novo), and Samara Martins (UP) have registered presidential candidacies with the TSE for 2026.

item.title: Crusoé: Renan Santos provoca Janja e faz live no Discord
item.description: Candidate Renan Santos provoked First Lady Janja by announcing his next live stream will be on Discord, in response to her appeal against the platform. He suggested that since Janja chose Discord as an enemy, his live will also be held there.

item.title: Fachin nega pedido de Flávio para declarar Moraes suspeito no caso Dark Horse
item.description: Supreme Federal Court President Edson Fachin rejected Flávio Bolsonaro's request to declare Alexandre de Moraes biased in the Dark Horse case, stating that the rapporteur is now André Mendonça. The decision was endorsed by the PGR and the case was formally closed on June 6. Flávio Bolsonaro is accused of seeking R$134 million from Daniel Vorcaro to fund a film about Jair Bolsonaro, with allegations that part of the money financed actions against Brazilian authorities.

item.title: Senado dos EUA aprova indicação de Trump para embaixador no Brasil
item.description: The U.S. Senate confirmed Daniel President Trump's nominee, Daniel Perez, as ambassador to Brazil, but the Lula administration will delay granting agrément until after the 2026 election runoff. In response, the Trump administration revoked the visa of Brazilian Ambassador to Washington, Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti. The Planalto states it does not intend to reject the nomination but insists on following diplomatic protocol by requiring agrément prior to U.S. legislative approval.

item.title: Apoio de Trump a Flávio Bolsonaro não amplia intenção de voto, mostra Quaest. Mais brasileiros querem independência dos EUA
item.description: Donald Trump's declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in August did not increase his voting intention, which remained at 29% from June to August, according to the Genial/Quaest poll. For a majority of voters (51%), Trump's endorsement would have a negative effect: 35% say it increases their likelihood of voting for Lula, and 16% say it would lead them to support another candidate. Only 15% said the alliance with the U.S. leader would make no difference.

item.title: Lula volta a reclamar de avião presidencial em reunião com militares
item.description: Lula again complained about the condition of the presidential aircraft during a meeting with the military leadership last week. The president expressed dissatisfaction with the state of the aircraft used for official travel, according to sources from the exclusive report. Full access to the article requires a subscriber login and registration.

item.title: TSE determina bloqueio das contas de Fábio Faria, ex-ministro de Bolsonaro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ordered the blocking of accounts belonging to former minister Fábio Faria due to non-payment of a fine imposed for publishing content against Lula (PT) during the 2022 electoral campaign. The measure aims to enforce the sanction issued by electoral justice. The blockade remains in effect while Faria awaits a final ruling on the case.

item.title: ‘Judiciário virou um poder incendiário’, diz Zema em novo ataque ao STF
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo Party's pre-candidate for president, harshly criticized the Supreme Federal Court (STF), claiming the Judiciary has ceased to be a moderating power and become 'incendiary', fueling political tension. He accused justices of enjoying untouchable privileges, even suggesting a 'serial killer' judge would face no consequences under current laws. Zema also advocated for reforms in judicial appointments, such as a triple list and minimum age of 60, and reiterated his criticism of Justice Gilmar Mendes over a defamation lawsuit.

item.title: O fogo amigo do PT no caso Marcola e a bomba para Lula nas investigações sobre Lulinha
item.description: The Marcola case, involving Lula’s former chief of staff, has created internal strain within the PT after it was revealed he received R$ 249,000 from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, close to Lulinha. While Marcola claims the money was a personal loan, suspicions suggest it was intended to benefit Lulinha’s interests in government. The leak is described as 'friendly fire' from within the PT, reflecting internal tensions over his growing influence in Lula’s campaign.

item.title: Ex-BBB Matteus se declara branco ao TSE após polêmica com cota racial
item.description: Former BBB contestant Matteus Amaral declared himself white to the TSE following controversy over alleged racial quota fraud for admission to IFFAR in 2014. He claims the enrollment was made by third parties without his knowledge and regrets any impression of improper benefit. Matteus is running for federal deputy in 2026 under the Progressistas party.

item.title: “O PT tem sido conivente com o avanço do narcotráfico”, diz Caiado
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado accused the Workers' Party (PT) of being complicit in the advance of drug trafficking in Brazil, citing insecurity in Rio de Janeiro’s streets as evidence. The statement was made during a GloboNews and g1 sabatina on Friday, February 7. Caiado implied that the PT’s inaction enables organized crime to grow.

item.title: Candidata a deputada, Val Marchiori declara R$ 49 milhões em bens
item.description: Val Marchiori, a socialite and former model known for appearing on the reality show 'Rich Women,' officially registered her candidacy for federal deputy from São Paulo in the 2026 elections and declared assets exceeding R$ 49 million to the TSE. Her declared assets include a house valued at R$ 48 million, R$ 800,000 in jewelry and artworks, plus bank deposits and a 50% stake in company shares. This is her first time running for elected office.

item.title: O caos e a preocupação nos bastidores da escolha do nome para vice de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The last-minute selection of Alfredo Gaspar as Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate replaced the expected choice of Rogério Marinho, forming a pure PL ticket that excluded women and Centrão party leaders. Gaspar's inclusion raised immediate concerns due to unresolved allegations of sexual abuse of a minor, which he denies, and the campaign's failure to conduct proper vetting. While Gaspar may serve as a political asset due to his role in investigating pension fraud, his controversial background now poses a significant liability.

item.title: Entrevista ao g1 e à GloboNews: Caiado propõe criar polícia conjunta com países sul-americanos para combater o crime organizado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) proposed the creation of a joint police force with ten South American countries to combat international organized crime, modeled after Europol’s cross-border policing framework. He also advocated deploying the Brazilian Armed Forces (Army, Navy, and Air Force) to reoccupy territories controlled by criminal factions, stating their role is not to arrest but to resolve territorial occupation.
